source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
EdgeCore's AS02 in Sterling, Virginia publishes 114 MW of IT capacity and 685,000 square feet of technical space, making it the fourth-largest facility by disclosed megawattage in a state with 376 mapped data centers.

The 114 MW is a power envelope, not a compute count. EdgeCore publishes no rack count, no accelerator count, and no tenant names, so any figure for those is an outside estimate. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 114 MW implies roughly 2,850 racks. At 100 kW per rack, a denser liquid-cooled assumption, it implies roughly 1,140 racks. Both are arithmetic applied to the published megawatt figure, not claims by the operator.

The only certification listed is LEED, which describes the building's environmental performance and says nothing about power redundancy, cooling method, or network fabric. None of those are published. A reader should not treat the LEED listing or the megawatt figure as evidence about what workloads the campus can host or who occupies it.

Virginia is the largest state in this mapping by a wide margin, and 29 of its 376 facilities publish a megawatt figure. Those 29 account for 2,563.4 MW, so AS02 alone is a meaningful share of what can actually be counted. The gap between 376 mapped sites and 29 with published numbers is the central fact: most of the Northern Virginia buildout is invisible in capacity terms because operators do not disclose figures.
